word_count: A word is a maximal run of Unicode letters. An apostrophe between letters stays inside the word. Digits, underscores, and hyphens are boundaries. The count covers each file as stored, including its id line and headings.
token_count: Each file is encoded on its own with tiktoken, as exact UTF-8 text, with no chat wrapper and no added special tokens. Work, tier, and corpus totals are sums of those file counts, not the token count of the files concatenated.

works.title: Lectures and Fragments
works.license_basis: Translated by Blake Raymond from Otto Hense, C. Musonii Rufi Reliquiae (Teubner, Leipzig, 1905). works.numbering: Hense's 1905 numbering, also used by Lutz. Lectures I-XXI are musonius.rufus.N, with the split discourses as 13a, 13b, 15a, 15b, 18a, and 18b. Fragments XXII-LIII are musonius.rufus.22 through musonius.rufus.53 in one file. One file per lecture. The spurious Letter to Pancratides and the four letters in Philostratus are omitted.

works.author: Seneca
works.title: Natural Questions
works.license_basis: John Clarke's translation was published in 1910, before the 1930 United States public-domain cutoff. The translator is identified as John Clarke, Lecturer in Education at Aberdeen, born in 1853 or 1854 and died in 1939. That identification matches the 1910 title page to a family genealogy; it is a judgment call, not a national-biography entry. On that death date, the Canadian life-plus-50 term expired at the end of 1989, before the 30 December 2022 extension to life-plus-70, and the copyright was not revived. Taken from Project Gutenberg ebook 76392. The Gutenberg header, footer, and trademark language were removed, as were Archibald Geikie's notes, Clarke's own notes, the index, running heads, marginal section numbers, and bracketed note markers. Included only as an optional physics text.
works.numbering: Clarke's own books and chapters. Ids are seneca.naturales_quaestiones.B.C, plus a preface passage where Clarke printed one (books 1, 3, and 4). His book 4 is the book later editions divide into IVA and IVB; this corpus keeps Clarke's book, not that later split. Chapter counts are 17, 59, 30, 13, 18, 32, and 32.

missing.reason: The first complete English translation is Alan C. Bowen and Robert B. Todd, Cleomedes' Lectures on Astronomy (University of California Press, 2004), which is in copyright. No earlier complete English translation was found at Project Gutenberg, Wikisource, or Perseus. Cleomedes was optional and is omitted.

missing.author: Early Stoics
missing.title: Collected fragments (Zeno, Cleanthes, Chrysippus, and others)
missing.reason: There is no public-domain English collection of the early Stoic fragments. Von Arnim's Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta is Greek and Latin. A. A. Long and D. N. Sedley, The Hellenistic Philosophers (1987), and Brad Inwood and Lloyd P. Gerson's Stoic sourcebooks are in copyright. Early Stoic doctrine is present in this corpus only where a public-domain translation already contains it: Diogenes Laertius book 7, Cicero's On Ends book 3, On Duties, and On the Nature of the Gods book 2, and Cleanthes' Hymn to Zeus. Those works are not a substitute for a fragment collection.

missing.author: Cicero
missing.title: On Fate
missing.reason: C. D. Yonge's public-domain translation is in The Treatises of M. T. Cicero (Bohn, 1853, with later printings), but the copies located are page scans. No clean Project Gutenberg, Wikisource, or Standard Ebooks transcription was found, and this corpus does not ship OCR. Stoic arguments about fate are still present in On the Nature of the Gods book 2, On Ends book 3, and Diogenes Laertius book 7.
